The last step I tried was to build a standalone binary with Bun, excluding the optional `react-devtools-core` dependency via the `--external` flag. The build succeeded and produced a large executable, but when I ran it I immediately got the same runtime error:

```
error: Cannot find package 'react-devtools-core' from '/$bunfs/root/glint'
```

So even though the bundler was told to treat `react-devtools-core` as external, something in the bundled code still tries to `require` it at runtime. That tells me the import is probably hard‑coded somewhere in Ink’s compiled source, not just a top‑level import that Bun can treat as external. Ink is the library that powers the TUI, and its source includes a `devtools.js` file that conditionally loads React DevTools. If that file is being required unconditionally, the binary will fail when the package isn’t present.

My next move is to locate every place in Ink’s build output where the string “devtools” appears, to see how the module is being pulled in. I’ll grep through all the compiled JavaScript files under `node_modules/ink/build`, but I want to exclude the `devtools.js` file itself in the first pass, because that file will obviously contain the word “devtools” and isn’t helpful for finding the import sites. After listing those matches (limiting to the first few with `head`), I’ll also inspect the top of `devtools.js` directly to understand what it does—whether it conditionally requires `react-devtools-core` based on environment variables, and whether I can influence that at build time.

Therefore, the appropriate command is:

```
grep -rn "devtools" node_modules/ink/build/*.js | grep -v "devtools.js:" | head
echo ---
head -20 node_modules/ink/build/devtools.js
```

This will give me a concise view of all import points and the implementation of the devtools shim, which is the information I need before deciding how to adjust the build (e.g., patching Ink to skip the import, setting an env flag, or bundling a stub).
